title: Overexpose
description: A summer sky through a pine, developed live on colour negative film. Drag up to overexpose it by as much as three stops. A phone sensor would clip the clouds to flat white; the negative's long shoulder and the print paper's toe fold the light in instead, so the cobalt thins to powder blue, the shadows open into pastel, and the cumulus keep their shape all the way up. Halation and diffusion grow as the shadows they land on lift out of the toe.
intent: Genre spec idea 5, after Rinko Kawauchi's overexposed 6x6 colour (Utatane, Illuminance): show why film looks dreamy and digital looks cheap with one gesture, exposure, on real linear radiance through per-layer H&D curves and a print curve. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinko_Kawauchi
sources: HDRI: Tree Lined Driveway, Poly Haven, photographed by Dimitrios Savva, processed by Jarod Guest, CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/tree_lined_driveway (8k .hdr: https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/HDRIs/hdr/8k/tree_lined_driveway_8k.hdr). Worm's-eye view lying under the pines: stereographic projection, 116 deg field, pitched +76 deg towards the zenith at yaw +150 deg from the panorama centre, rolled -10 deg, 1536 px square. The sun is moved behind the top-centre pine. No camera aim can do that (in this HDRI it stands in open sky about 20 deg from the nearest crown, and turning the camera carries the crown along), so its disc, 16-ray diffraction star and aureole are painted out of the equirect, then the frame's open sky is fitted as an elevation gradient plus a radial term around the old sun, and only the radial term is moved to a new direction 2 deg inside that crown's lower edge, with the measured, ray-free circumsolar excess added there, on sky pixels only with a 1-2 px feather. Around the sun the crown is rebuilt as a hard silhouette at its own dark density, and needles on its open-sky edge in the sun's forward lobe get a thin (about 2 px) warm-white transmitted rim, scaled to outshine the sky beyond. The pale ghost the painted-out sun still left is removed in the camera frame: on open sky 10-48 deg from the new sun (thin cloud excluded by its whiteness against the fit), the sky is replaced by the fitted elevation gradient with no old-sun radial term, and the photograph's grain is re-added, matched in amplitude, grain size and channel correlation from open sky far from both suns. The sky therefore deepens away from the crown instead of paling towards an empty patch. Shipped as log2 radiance -8.5..+2.5 in 8 bits with TPDF dither (scene.webp), with the diffusion and halation blurs baked from the same radiance (optics.png). Bake: tools/depth/bakes/overexpose (desun.py, resun.py, bake_wormseye.py).
